newsitem.title: USA: Apple expected to post big quarterly loss.
newsitem.headline: Apple expected to post big quarterly loss.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc. could report a loss as big as $100 million for its fiscal third quarter amid plunging sales of its Macintosh computers, industry analysts said Monday.
It also looks unlikely Apple will return to profitability by the September quarter, as ousted Chairman Gilbert Amelio had told investors earlier this year, the analysts said.
Amelio's surprise resignation last week "certainly indicates that their earlier goal is not doable," said James Poyner, computer analyst at investment bank Oppenheimer & Co.
"The straw that broke the camel's back was when the board of directors realised that they're not going to turn around in the near term."
Apple will report its fiscal third-quarter results after the stock markets close on Wednesday.

For the quarter ended June 30 analysts expect Apple, based in Cupertino, Calif., to report a loss between $70 million and $100 million. In the same quarter a year ago, Apple reported a loss of $32 million.
The average per-share loss estimate is 61 cents, according to a recent survey by First Call, which tracks analyst projections.

Behind Apple's projected heavy losses is a sharp downturn in sales of its Macintosh computers, analysts said. Shipments of Macintosh computers plunged this spring, according to a survey of 1,100 dealers by market researcher Computer Intelligence.
The number of shipped Apple PCs dropped 44 percent in April and 38 percent in May, compared with shipments in the same months in 1996, said Matt Sargent, analyst at Computer Intelligence.
Analysts expect Apple to report revenue of about $1.8 billion, down 17 percent from the $2.18 billion reported in the same year-ago quarter.
"Officially, we're looking for $1.83 billion in revenue, which would mean a loss of $98 million, but I think it could be worse than that," said Jay Vleeschhouwer, analyst at Josephthal Lyon & Ross.

Amelio's resignation under pressure from the board last week immediately raised concerns that Apple's quarter would be a disaster. But company executives said Amelio's departure was not related to this quarter's results.

Apple executives also had said they expected the company to report a profit as early as the fiscal fourth quarter, which ends Sept. 30. But Fred Anderson, Apple chief financial officer, declined to say last week whether the company is still on track to do that.
"We're not in the business of making predictions any more," he told reporters.
